parts: Consumers are people who buy goods and services to satisfy their needs; we are all consumers regardless of age or education. Consumer education teaches what, where, when, how and how much to buy and how to use what is bought. What: products meeting needs and priorities and of good quality, after a market survey (brand name is the popular name of a product). How much: the right quantity for need, money and space. Where: retail shops, cooperative stores, showrooms, authorised dealers, wholesale markets. When: seasonal goods in season, others in off-season or genuine discount sales; avoid busy Sundays and evenings. How: cash (cheaper) or credit and instalments (costlier; check terms); ask for guarantee and warranty cards with the receipt. How to use: read instructions. Advantages: decide and choose intelligently, demand safe reliable goods at reasonable prices, stay alert against corrupt practices and take action when faced with a problem.

Price variation (wholesale markets are cheaper; packed goods cost more than loose; MRP includes the seller's commission; purchasing power and 'end-of-season' or stock clearance sales; overcharging by copying brand names, using the highest MRP of different states, selling loose items without labels). Adulteration and poor quality (adding or removing things to lower quality, intentional; e.g. harmful colours, stale ingredients; electric shocks from poor irons; shrinking fabric). Non-availability: hoarding and black marketing (artificial scarcity, e.g. petrol, butter and oil before the Budget). Defective weights and measures (bricks or stones as weights, hollow-bottomed weights, magnets under pans, meters not showing zero, dented measures and stretched fabric). Deceptive trade practices (small goods in large packets, low-quality goods in stylish wrappers, similar brand names, fake free gifts, selling expired or second-hand goods as new). Poor consumer guidance (salespersons recommend only stocked brands). Lack of standardised products and misuse of standardisation marks.

Solutions: market surveys, buy from Kendriya Bhandar, fair price shops, cooperative stores and reliable shops, take bills, receipts and guarantee cards, prefer packed and labelled goods, read labels (brand name, ingredients, net weight, MRP, expiry date, standardisation mark), refuse to pay more for scarce goods, reject irregular weights, avoid sales tricks, buy goods with guarantee and after-sales service and report cheating. Six consumer rights: safety, to be informed, to choose, to be heard, to redressal and to consumer education. Responsibilities: keep bills and guarantee cards, insist on standardised goods, avoid being carried away by sales talk, follow instructions, do not misuse services such as free home delivery, report cheating and avoid waste.

Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act (AGMARK for wheat flour, honey, ghee, spices); Drugs and Cosmetics Act; Prevention of Food Adulteration Act; Essential Commodities Act; MRTP Act (false advertisements, hoarding, black marketing); Standards of Weights and Measures Act; Fruit Products Order (FPO for jams, pickles, juices, squashes); Consumer Protection Act (CPA, COPRA: rights, quick and inexpensive redressal in District, State and National Consumer Redressal Forums); BIS Act (ISI mark for ghee, biscuits, detergent, pressure cooker, iron, immersion rod, geyser, LPG cylinders, paint). Marks: ISI (BIS), AGMARK (agricultural products, about 142), FPO (fruit and vegetable products), Wool Mark (pure wool), Eco Mark (environment friendly products), and the green dot (vegetarian) or red dot (non-vegetarian) in a square on food labels.

A label shows the name, net weight, brand, MRP, manufacturer's name and address, ingredients, use, directions, warnings, guarantee period, dates of manufacture and expiry and, for medicines, the dosage. Packaging protects from damage and adulteration, eases handling and attracts buyers. An advertisement should give correct information; judge the product by examining it. A consumer movement is the joint action of consumers against unfair practices; the Government has declared 15 March as Consumer Rights Day.
